extracted.intended_audience: Toastmasters contest chairs, chief judges, voting and tiebreaking judges, timers, counters, contestants, and club/district officers involved in organizing or participating in Toastmasters speech contests
extracted.subtask_description: Official rulebook for conducting and participating in Toastmasters speech contests (International, Evaluation, Humorous, Table Topics, Tall Tales, and Online) including eligibility, procedure, timing, judging, and contest administration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognized contest types policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Toastmasters International recognizes and supports the following official speech contests: International Speech Contest, Evaluation Contest, Humorous Speech Contest, Table Topics Contest, Tall Tales Contest, and Online Speech Contest. No other contest types, showcases, etc., can be conducted by Districts (including Areas and Divisions) and Provisional Districts (including Areas and Divisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Districts may conduct up to three (3) additional English contests and up to four (4) non-English contests per year (with approval processes and limits described). Non-English contests must follow the rules of the corresponding English contest and may not continue beyond the District level. Modifications to rules may only be made through administrative Protocol; safety exceptions by CEO only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest progression (club → area → division → district)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contests must originate at the club level and proceed through the Area, Division, and District levels, respectively. Only contests following this progression are permitted at Area, Division, and District levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All clubs are eligible to advance contestants to the Area level in all contests, regardless of contest language. Provisional Districts must follow same progression. The International Speech Contest is the only contest that proceeds beyond the District level to quarterfinals, semifinals, and the World Championship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and limits on non-English contests
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Speech Contest must only be conducted in English. Districts may conduct non-English contests (up to four) in a language selected and approved by the District Director/Executive Committee; non-English contests must not continue beyond the District level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A non-English contest using International Speech Contest rules must be titled with the language (e.g., 'Chinese Speech Contest') and must follow all rules including eligibility requirements. Districts are not permitted to conduct multilingual contests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: paid membership and good standing
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible to compete in any official Toastmasters speech contest, a member must be a paid member of a club in the Area, Division, and District in which they are competing; the club must be in good standing; new/dual/reinstated members must have dues and membership application current with World Headquarters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility must be maintained at all levels. If it is later determined a contestant was ineligible at any previous level, they must be disqualified even if corrected later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for International Speech Contest (education requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible to compete in the International Speech Contest, a member must have earned certificates of completion in Levels 1 and 2 of any path in the Toastmasters Pathways learning experience or earned a Distinguished Toastmaster award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a club chartered less than one year before the club contest, charter members may compete without this requirement provided the club officially chartered before the Area contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible categories for contestants
rubrics_metrics.description: A specified list of members are ineligible to compete in any Toastmasters speech contest, including: incumbent International Officers and Directors, Region Advisors or applicants, District officers whose terms expire June 30 (District Director, Program Quality Director, Club Growth Director, Administration Manager, Finance Manager, Public Relations Manager, Division Director, Area Director), International Officer/Director candidates, Immediate Past District Directors, candidates for upcoming District-elected positions, and members serving in certain contest official/presenter roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also the winner of the World Championship of Public Speaking is not eligible to compete again in the International Speech Contest at any level. Members in more than one club who meet eligibility may compete in each club's contest, but no contestant may compete in more than one Area contest of a given type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest official and judge eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be a chief judge, voting judge, or tiebreaking judge at a Toastmasters speech contest, individuals must meet eligibility requirements: at club level be a paid member; at Area/Division/District be a paid member for minimum six months, completed minimum six speech projects in Competent Communication manual or earned Pathways Levels 1 and 2 (with transitional rules), and be physically present at the contest (exceptions for Online contest officials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For International Quarterfinals/Semifinals/World Championship, judges must be paid members for at least six months, be Advanced Toastmaster Bronze/Advanced Communicator Bronze or have completed at least one Pathways path, and have previous contest judging experience. Chief judge, voting judges, and tiebreaking judge must not be members of any club in which a contestant is a member at certain levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical presence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each contestant must be physically present to compete beyond the club level. Participation by audio, video, or other remote technology is not permitted beyond the club level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: participants in the International Speech Contest Quarterfinals and the Online Speech Contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and composition of contest officials by level
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies minimum officials per contest level (club, Area, Division, District, International Quarterfinals, Semifinals, World Championship), including number of voting judges, tiebreaking judge, chief judge, counters, timers, and restrictions (e.g., chief judge and judges must not be members of clubs with contestants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Club contests: contest chair, chief judge, at least five voting judges, a tiebreaking judge, two counters, two timers; Division contests: equal number of voting judges from each Area or min seven; District contests: equal number from each Division or min seven, three counters, two timers; International Quarterfinals/Semifinals/World Championship require nine or more voting judges, specific chief judge appointments, and strict conflict-of-interest rules. Voting judges must remain anonymous when practical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge materials and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each voting judge receives the appropriate Judge’s Guide and Ballot for the contest type; all voting judges and the tiebreaking judge receive the Judge’s Certification of Eligibility and Code of Ethics which must be signed and returned to the chief judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists item numbers for judge guides by contest type (e.g., International Item 1172, Humorous Item 1191).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiebreaking judge protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief judge selects a tiebreaking judge whose identity is secret, who does not attend the judges' briefing, and who receives a Tiebreaking Judge’s Guide and Ballot before the contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tiebreaking judges receive type-specific tiebreaking guides (item numbers stated). The tiebreaking ballot is used only in event of ties in the counting room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot completion and validity
rubrics_metrics.description: In order for a ballot to be valid, judges shall complete their ballots by entering their choices for first, second, and third place, sign and print their names on the ballot. E-signatures are acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting judges discreetly provide the bottom portion of the ballot to ballot counters; the top portion is not provided and must be discreetly discarded by the judge. Tiebreaking judge provides bottom portion to the chief judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring and tabulation (3–2–1 points)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the Counter’s Tally Sheet, each contestant receives points for being ranked first, second, or third on a voting judge’s ballot: Three (3) points for first, Two (2) points for second, One (1) point for third.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ballot counters compute total points for each contestant, verify totals among counters, rank contestants by total points. In event of a tie, chief judge consults tiebreaking judge’s ballot; tied contestant highest-ranked by tiebreaker gains the contested place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and disposal of ballots and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: All ballots, Counter’s Tally Sheet forms, and Time Record Sheets are considered confidential. After winners are announced, the chief judge will destroy all ballots, the time record, and the tally sheet; contest forms must be disposed of in a way that maintains complete confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chief judge keeps ballots and tally sheet until after winners announced; do not discuss details of protests/disqualifications with contestants (except eligibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing speaking positions and contestant briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the contest, contestants are briefed on the rules by the contest chair and then draw for speaking position with the contest chair. For Online contests, speaking position can be established using a randomization tool that is screenshared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If contestant is absent from briefing, alternate may attend in their place; rules on late arrival and waiving briefing are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaking area and equipment availability
rubrics_metrics.description: All contestants will speak from the platform or area designated by the contest chair. A lectern/podium will be available but optional. If amplification is necessary, fixed and portable microphones must be available; all equipment must be available for contestants to practice with prior to the contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Online contests, speaking participants are responsible for their own equipment; contestants are responsible for arranging preferred setup quietly before introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speech subject selection rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject of International, Humorous, Tall Tales, and Online contest speeches must be selected by the contestant. Table Topics subjects are determined by the contest chair. Evaluation Contest subjects are limited to oral evaluations of the test speaker’s speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contestants must create their own substantially original speeches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and external content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants must create their own speeches, each must be substantially original. Twenty-five percent or less of the speech may be devoted to quoting, paraphrasing, or referencing another person’s content; any quoted/paraphrased/referenced content must be identified during the speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before all contests, every contestant must certify in writing to the chief judge that the content of their speech is or will be substantially original using the Speaker’s Certification of Eligibility and Originality (Item 1183).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on referencing other contestants
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants must not reference another contestant, or a speech presented by another contestant, during their speech at the same contest in which they are competing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests regarding reference to another contestant/speech are allowed and governed by protest rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing devices, signaling, and official timekeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Two (2) timers are appointed (one stopwatch, one signaling device) whose signals must be in full view of each contestant; the stopwatch timer maintains and delivers official elapsed time on the Speech Contest Time Record Sheet (Item 1175).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A minimum backup timer is required for Online contests. The signaling device must provide green/yellow/red signals at contest-specific times (detailed in timing rules). Any visually impaired contestant may request an alternate warning signal. In event of signal/timing equipment technical failure, speaker allowed 30 seconds extra overtime before disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules and disqualification thresholds by contest type
rubrics_metrics.description: Speeches must conform to timing guidelines per contest type. Examples: International/Humorous/Online: 5–7 minutes; disqualified if <4:30 or >7:30 (disqualification at 7:31). Table Topics: 1–2 minutes; disqualified if <1:00 or >2:30. Evaluation: 2–3 minutes; disqualified if <1:30 or >3:30. Tall Tales: 3–5 minutes; disqualified if <2:30 or >5:30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timers must not consider fractions of a second. A contestant is not 'qualified' until the lower threshold is reached and not disqualified until reaching the upper+1 second threshold as specified. Specific green/yellow/red times per contest are provided in rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start-of-speech timing protocol (audiovisual confirmation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon being introduced, the contestant must proceed immediately to the speaking position and say, 'Thank you, Contest Chair.' If audiovisual equipment is functional, contest chair responds 'You're welcome.' Timing begins with the contestant's next definite verbal or nonverbal communication with the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If audiovisual equipment is not functional, the contest chair pauses the contest to allow corrections; Online contestants allowed 10 minutes to correct equipment; failure to correct continues contest with next contestant. Speaker should not delay contest unnecessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protests: scope, lodging, and resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Protests are limited to eligibility, originality, and reference to another contestant or another contestant’s speech and must only be lodged by voting judges and/or contestants. Any protest must be lodged with the chief judge and/or contest chair prior to the contest being adjourned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chief judge, contest chair, voting judges, and contestants must not consider protests from audience members. Before disqualification for originality or referencing another contestant/speech, contestant must be given opportunity to respond; a majority of voting judges must concur with disqualification. All protests must be resolved before adjournment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting room procedures and tie resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: All ballots are tabulated by ballot counters and chief judge in a private counting room; use Counter’s Tally Sheet. Points assigned per ranking (3/2/1); totals verified by all ballot counters. In event of tie, chief judge consults tiebreaking judge’s ballot and the tied contestant with highest ranking on tiebreaking ballot gains the contested place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ballots and tally sheet are kept until winners announced; ballots counted twice to ensure accuracy; finalists/advancing contestants sometimes announced without placement (quarterfinals/semifinals rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement of winners protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: After contestant interviews, the contest chair announces winners. In contests with 3+ participants, announce third, second, then first (reverse order). In contests with fewer than 3 participants, announce second (if applicable) then first. Winners must be announced prior to end of event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple contests at one event, each contest must be officially adjourned before beginning next contest. For International Quarterfinals and Semifinals advancing contestants will be announced in no particular order (placement not announced). Prior to announcing results, chair must announce number of time disqualifications but not name contestants involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest chair responsibilities (planning and conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contest chair duties include planning contest budget, arranging venue/online platform/A-V equipment, conducting publicity, ensuring bills paid, verifying contestant eligibility, ensuring provided audiovisual equipment works, briefing chief judge/voting judges/timers/counters, ensuring ballots are counted carefully, and presenting awards professionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair may have a committee but remains responsible. Must notify contest officials and contestants of time/place and provide information packets weeks in advance; ensure trademark rules for awards (do not put Toastmasters logo on awards not purchased from World HQ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contestant pre-contest and in-contest responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants must select topics (where applicable), prepare substantially original speeches, attend briefing and rehearsal, inform chair of props, test equipment (Online), set up props during one-minute silence prior to introduction, say 'Thank you, Contest Chair' after introduction, begin when chair replies 'You’re welcome', check timing signals and wrap up when red, and remove props immediately after speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By signing Speaker’s Certification, contestants certify they understand eligibility and originality rules. Props helpers permitted but contest officials are not responsible for handling props.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge’s briefing and judge-room protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Chief judge conducts judge’s briefing for voting judges, counters, and timers; distribute materials including list of contestants in speaking order, Judge’s Guide and Ballot, Speech Contest Rulebook, Judge’s Certification, and training materials for online platform; instruct judges on procedures to mitigate unexpected challenges and seating proximity to contest area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International/Evaluation/Humorous/Table Topics/Tall Tales judge briefings may be in person or online; Online contest judge briefing must be online. Brief ballot counters and timers on tally sheet and time record; provide stopwatch; ensure judges comfortable with online platform where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and forms requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific contest materials are required/available for roles: Speaker’s Certification of Eligibility and Originality (Item 1183), Speech Contest Time Record Sheet (Item 1175), Judge’s Guides and Ballots per contest type, Judge’s Certification of Eligibility and Code of Ethics (Item 1170), Counter’s Tally Sheet (Item 1176), Notification of Contest Winner (Item 1182), Results Form (Item 1168), Speech Contestant Profile (Item 1189), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speech contest materials are available free at toastmasters.org/Speech-Contest-Kits; use of correct forms supports rule compliance and recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external voting systems prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of external voting systems is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ballots and tabulation must follow the prescribed Counter’s Tally Sheet and internal procedures; electronic or third-party voting systems not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of disruptions and rescheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: If a contest must be paused or rescheduled due to disruption, partially completed speeches may be allowed to begin again from the start during rescheduled contest. Contest officials must send all partially completed forms (Judge’s Guide and Ballot, Time Record Sheet, etc.) to the chief judge to be stored until the rescheduled contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contest officials should have a method of private communication to pause the contest; timers/counters should secure their records in envelopes if physical forms are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timers' visibility and warning signals accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Timer's signaling device must be in full view of each contestant but not obvious to the audience; timers must provide warning signals clearly visible to speakers. Any visually impaired contestant is permitted to request and must be granted a form of warning signal of their own choosing (buzzer, bell, person announcing times, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Online contests, ensure judges/viewers are in locations where interruptions are unlikely and have reliable internet; provide backup timer if necessary for technical issues.
